newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Most Cimpor shares for foreigners - paper.
newsitem.headline: Most Cimpor shares for foreigners - paper.

text.p: Most shares in the second stage privatisation of Portuguese cement producer Cimpor-Cimentos de Portugal next month should be sold to foreign investors, the president of the company was quoted as saying.
"Forty percent of the shares for sale should be for national investors and the rest for foreigners," Antonio Sousa Gomes told Publico newspaper in an interview.

The Socialist government of Prime Minister Antonio Guterres plans to sell off 45 percent of Cimpor in a second stage privatisation expected in the middle of October. The government will retain 35 percent.
Sousa Gomes said the present Cimpor share price could fall eventually as small investors and employees who buy the shares at a discount later sell them at a profit.
Asked if the Cimpor share price was high, Sousa Gomes said: "Yes. And as small investors and employees, among others, have access to shares with a discount, this will certainly lead to a small drop."
Cimpor closed on Lisbon bouse on Friday at 3,380 escudos.

Sousa Gomes said that unlike the first stage privatisation of 20 percent of Cimpor in which no large investors emerged, this time a major investor could take up to a 10 percent stake, the limit that may be held by a single investor.
"In the second stage, some entity could appear that wants to take a more important position, but there is a 10 percent limit," he said.
"The state will continue as the shareholder of reference, with the most voting power," he added.
